title: I Become a Student
subtitle: A claim about education → chosen interests → conflicting authorities → a new view of history → a task for youth
question: What turns a university student into an independent learner?
thesis: Steffens becomes a student when curiosity turns conflicting accounts into research questions and learning matters more than credentials.
thesisZh: 当好奇心使史家的分歧变成自己的研究问题、求知超过求文凭时，斯蒂芬斯才真正成为学生。
conclusion: The lasting achievement is a method of inquiry and the discovery that young people have unfinished intellectual work to do.
conclusionZh: 真正的收获是学会探究的方法，并发现尚未完成的学术工作正等待青年参与。

design.pattern: Intellectual turning-point path: interest → doubt → discovery, enclosed by the opening claim and closing vocation
design.rationale: 以第3—4段“权威分歧→历史成为研究领域”为转折中心，呈现个人求知变化，不做通用学习步骤。

stages.title: A university education is possible, but not automatic
stages.summary: He defines education as the capacity and drive to learn, even when independent study threatens the degree.
stages.summaryZh: 他把教育界定为学习的能力与动力，即使独立学习可能妨碍取得学位。

nodes.label: What counts as education
nodes.text: A degree matters less than the [[capacity and drive to learn]].
nodes.zh: 文凭不如学习的能力与动力重要。

nodes.label: The institutional obstacle
nodes.text: Interested, methodical study requires finding a way around the college system of [[mind-fixing]].
nodes.zh: 有兴趣、有方法的学习，需要摆脱大学体系对思想的定型。

compact.label: Beyond the Degree
compact.keywords: Learning matters more than credentials
compact.zh: 超越文凭：学习本身更重要

balanced.label: Education Beyond the Degree
balanced.summary: Steffens values the capacity and drive to learn above a degree, even when independent study challenges university routines.
balanced.zh: 斯蒂芬斯认为，学习的能力与动力比文凭更重要，即使独立求学会与大学的惯常要求发生冲突。

stages.title: Interest draws separate subjects into a historical question
stages.summary: He chooses subjects that interest him and discovers that history can illuminate questions raised by his other reading.
stages.summaryZh: 他专攻自己感兴趣的学科，并发现历史能帮助解释其他阅读提出的问题。

nodes.label: Choose a focus
nodes.text: Instead of giving every prescribed course equal attention, he [[specializes]] in the subjects that interest him most.
nodes.zh: 他不对所有规定课程平均用力，而是专攻最感兴趣的学科。

nodes.label: Require a reason to remember
nodes.text: His “bad memory” resists isolated names and dates; he needs [[understanding]] and an intellectual purpose.
nodes.zh: 他所谓的“坏记性”排斥孤立的人名和日期；他需要理解内容，并知道学习的意义。

nodes.label: A new reason to study history
nodes.text: Literature, philosophy and political economy reveal connections that make him want to [[dig deeper]] into history.
nodes.zh: 文学、哲学和政治经济学让他看到学科之间的联系，激起深入研究历史的愿望。

compact.label: Follow Curiosity
compact.keywords: Other subjects spark historical questions
compact.zh: 追随好奇：其他学科引出历史问题

balanced.label: Interest Gives History Meaning
balanced.summary: Literature, philosophy and political economy lead him toward history because it can illuminate questions he already cares about.
balanced.detail: Understanding gives names and dates a reason to matter.
balanced.zh: 文学、哲学与政治经济学的阅读使他转向历史，因为历史能解释他已经关心的问题；有了理解，人名与日期才有意义。

stages.title: Extra reading unsettles the idea of settled knowledge
stages.summary: Comparing assigned books and additional authorities exposes disagreement, giving his existing curiosity an unresolved historical problem to pursue.
stages.summaryZh: 比较指定读物与其他权威著作揭示了观点分歧，让他原有的好奇心找到了一个尚待解答的历史问题。

nodes.label: The first discrepancy
nodes.text: The two required books [[differ]] on several points, and further authorities disagree too.
nodes.zh: 两本必读书在若干问题上存在分歧，其他权威著作也各执一词。

nodes.label: Keep looking
nodes.text: The librarian and Professor Jones supply more references, but extra reading [[deepens the mystery]].
nodes.zh: 图书管理员和琼斯教授提供了更多参考书，但继续阅读反而加深了疑问。

nodes.label: A different motive
nodes.text: He is not trying to be a good boy: he is a [[curious boy]] searching for an answer.
nodes.zh: 他并非为了成为听话的好学生，而是出于好奇寻找答案。

compact.label: Authorities Disagree
compact.keywords: More reading deepens the mystery
compact.zh: 权威分歧：读得越多，疑问越深

balanced.label: Authorities Raise New Questions
balanced.summary: Assigned books disagree, and further reading deepens the mystery, turning his curiosity toward an answer still to be discovered.
balanced.zh: 指定教材彼此矛盾，继续阅读反而加深疑问，使他出于好奇追寻尚待发现的答案。

stages.title: Uncertainty opens a field in which he can participate
stages.summary: Historians’ disagreements make history an open field for investigation, where original evidence can challenge accepted accounts.
stages.summaryZh: 史家的分歧使历史成为开放的探究领域，原始证据可以用来检验公认的叙述。
stages.relation: turns disagreement into a research opportunity

nodes.label: A change in his role
nodes.text: History becomes a [[field for research]] in which he, too, can make discoveries.
nodes.zh: 历史成为一个他也能参与并有所发现的研究领域。

nodes.label: A tentative challenge
nodes.text: He suspects the Constitution’s authors did not seek democracy and imagines writing its history, but [[does not write it]].
nodes.zh: 他怀疑美国宪法的制定者并不追求民主，曾设想重写其历史，但没有完成这项写作。

nodes.label: The standard for inquiry
nodes.text: Disagreeing authorities point him toward [[original documents]] and other decisive evidence across his history courses.
nodes.zh: 各门历史课中权威意见的分歧，使他意识到需要重新查找原始文献与其他确凿证据。

compact.label: History Becomes Inquiry
compact.keywords: Test accepted accounts against original evidence
compact.zh: 历史成为探究：用原始证据检验已有说法

balanced.label: History Opens to Inquiry
balanced.summary: Conflicting accounts make history an open field for discovery, where original documents can test what historians claim.
balanced.detail: He doubts the founders’ democratic aims; his planned history remains unwritten.
balanced.zh: 互相冲突的记载使历史成为可以探索的领域，原始文献可以检验史家的说法。他怀疑制宪者是否意在建立民主政府，但未写成自己设想的历史。

stages.title: Recognition matters less than the method he has found
stages.summary: He values his growing method of inquiry and sees the rewriting of history as work awaiting young learners.
stages.summaryZh: 他珍视逐渐掌握的研究方法，并把重写历史看作等待青年学习者承担的工作。

nodes.label: The personal gain
nodes.text: What matters is learning a [[method of studying history]], rather than satisfying vanity.
nodes.zh: 重要的是掌握研究历史的方法，而非满足虚荣心。

nodes.label: The invitation
nodes.text: History is crying out to be [[rewritten]]: there is something for youth to do.
nodes.zh: 历史正等待重新书写：青年有值得投入的事情可做。

compact.label: Work for Youth
compact.keywords: Learn the method; help rewrite history
compact.zh: 青年的使命：掌握方法，参与重写历史

balanced.label: Unfinished Work for Youth
balanced.summary: He values his emerging method of study and recognizes that rewriting history gives young people meaningful work to do.
balanced.zh: 他珍视逐渐掌握的研究方法，并意识到重写历史为青年提供了值得投入的工作。

compact.core: Curiosity turns a student into an independent learner
compact.coreZh: 好奇心让学生成为独立的求知者

balanced.route: Education beyond credentials → chosen interests → conflicting authorities → inquiry → intellectual purpose

cards.title: Topic · University education
cards.zh: 文章以大学教育为话题，指出真正的学习虽少见，却可能实现；个人经历将说明如何做到。

cards.title: Thesis · Independent learning
cards.zh: 真正的教育是学习的能力和动力；独立、有方法地求学，要突破思想定型，价值超过文凭。

cards.title: Study habits
cards.zh: 原图的四个学习分支：按兴趣专攻、广泛自主阅读、在理解基础上记忆，以及把文学、哲学和政治经济学的问题带入历史。

children.text: History illuminates questions from other subjects

cards.title: References → questions
cards.zh: 先向教授索取参考书目，再比较指定教材，向图书管理员和教授寻找其他权威。各书分歧使疑问深化；他的动力是好奇。

cards.title: Evidence → possible research
cards.zh: 回到原始文献，提出可以检验的设想。他曾怀疑制宪者并非意在建立民主政府，并计划写制宪史，但没有完成这项写作。

cards.title: Value recap
cards.zh: 真正的收获是研究方法和求知动力，而非虚荣或文凭。

cards.title: Call to youth
cards.zh: 历史等待重新书写；青年有值得投入的工作。

title: Should the Robots Be Taxed?
subtitle: A proposed remedy → historical and social context → tax and speed objections → responsibility during transition
question: Does automation call for a robot tax, or a different response to the pain of transition?
thesis: The author treats robots as the latest tools of automation and questions the tax rationale while acknowledging uneven gains and painful adjustment.
thesisZh: 作者把机器人视为自动化进程中的新工具，质疑征税的理由，同时承认收益不均与转型的痛苦。
conclusion: Automation repeatedly changes work; its painful transitions call for empathy, compassion and social responsibility.
conclusionZh: 自动化不断改变工作的形态；痛苦的转型阶段需要同理心、关怀与社会责任。

design.pattern: Argument fan: a policy question branches into historical context, tax revenue and transition speed, then converges on social responsibility
design.rationale: 把税收与变化速度作为两个回应分支；历史和社会变化提供背景，结尾承认代价，不把类比画成政策证明。

stages.title: Robot taxes and basic income enter the debate
stages.summary: Gates’s proposal and a European draft report connect robot taxation and basic income with fears of unemployment.
stages.summaryZh: 盖茨的提议和欧洲的一份报告草案，将机器人税与基本收入同失业担忧联系起来。

nodes.label: Tax robot owners
nodes.text: Gates’s proposal gains attention; a draft report suggests taxing robot owners or requiring [[social security]] contributions.
nodes.zh: 盖茨的提议引发关注；一份报告草案建议向机器人所有者征税或要求其缴纳社会保障费用。

nodes.label: Protect displaced workers
nodes.text: A [[basic income]] or guaranteed welfare program is suggested as protection against unemployment.
nodes.zh: 基本收入或有保障的福利计划，被提出作为应对失业的保护措施。

compact.label: The Proposal
compact.keywords: Robot taxes and basic income
compact.zh: 政策提议：机器人税与基本收入

balanced.label: A Proposed Safety Net
balanced.summary: Robot taxes and basic income are proposed to protect people whose jobs may be replaced by machines.
balanced.zh: 机器人税与基本收入被提出，用来保护工作可能被机器取代的人。

stages.title: New tools reorganize work, but people can be left behind
stages.summary: The author compares robots with earlier tools: work changes across generations, while displaced workers face a lag.
stages.summaryZh: 作者把机器人与以往工具相比较：工作在代际更替中变化，但失业者会遭遇转型滞后。

nodes.label: A change in production
nodes.text: Textile factories replace cottage work with fixed hours, shared machinery and a greater [[division of labor]].
nodes.zh: 纺织工厂以固定工时、集中使用机器和更细的劳动分工，取代家庭作坊式生产。

nodes.label: Different jobs, different generations
nodes.text: Weavers’ families found factory jobs; factory workers’ children [[might]] become knowledge workers.
nodes.zh: 织工的家人曾在工厂找到工作；工厂工人的孩子将来也许会成为知识工作者。

nodes.label: The qualification
nodes.text: New opportunities do not remove the [[lag]]: some people will be left behind.
nodes.zh: 新机会并不能消除转型的滞后：一部分人仍会掉队。

compact.label: Earlier Automation
compact.keywords: New jobs emerge; displaced workers lag
compact.zh: 历史经验：新工作出现，失业者仍会掉队

balanced.label: Automation Has a History
balanced.summary: The author places robots within a long history of tools reshaping work, while admitting that some workers fall behind.
balanced.detail: Weavers’ families found factory work; later generations may gain different jobs.
balanced.zh: 作者把机器人放入工具不断改变工作的历史中，同时承认有人会在转型中掉队。织工的家人曾进入工厂，后代也许会从事另一种工作。

stages.title: The changes extend to families, resources and unequal benefits
stages.summary: The essay broadens from jobs to demographic change, possible resource adaptation and the uneven distribution of automation’s benefits.
stages.summaryZh: 文章从就业扩展到人口变化、可能的资源适应，以及自动化收益分配不均。

nodes.label: Families and ageing
nodes.text: The author links changing work to falling [[birth rates]] and notes lower marriage rates and an ageing population.
nodes.zh: 作者把工作变化与出生率下降联系起来，并指出结婚率降低和人口老龄化的趋势。

nodes.label: A possible adaptation
nodes.text: One theory proposes that future generations facing scarce resources will learn to [[conserve]] them.
nodes.zh: 一种理论认为，未来世代面对资源紧缺，会学会节约资源。

nodes.label: Productive capacity, unequal gains
nodes.text: Education, research and health can benefit from spare capacity, but income gains have favored [[developed nations]].
nodes.zh: 释放出的人力可促进教育、研究和健康，但收入增长更多地惠及发达国家。

compact.label: Wider Changes
compact.keywords: Ageing, resources, unequal gains
compact.zh: 更广的变化：老龄化、资源与收益不均

balanced.label: Wider Social Changes
balanced.summary: The discussion extends to family changes, ageing and productive spare capacity, while acknowledging uneven economic gains.
balanced.zh: 讨论进一步涉及家庭变化、人口老龄化和富余人力的利用，同时承认经济收益分配不均。

stages.title: The tax argument shifts attention from wages to other revenues
stages.summary: The author argues that lost wage taxes must be considered alongside corporate profits, robot investment and new jobs elsewhere.
stages.summaryZh: 作者认为，工资税的减少应与企业利润、机器人投资以及其他地方的新岗位一并考虑。

nodes.label: The concern
nodes.text: Robots receive no wages, raising concern about a loss of [[tax revenue]].
nodes.zh: 机器人不领取工资，因此引发税收减少的担忧。

nodes.label: The author’s reply
nodes.text: The author argues that higher [[corporate profits]] and jobs involved in making robots generate other taxes.
nodes.zh: 作者认为，更高的企业利润和制造机器人相关的岗位会带来其他税收。

nodes.label: A geographical complication
nodes.text: New jobs and taxes may arise in [[different regions or countries]], creating a source of conflict.
nodes.zh: 新的岗位和税收可能出现在其他地区或国家，由此产生矛盾。

compact.label: Revenue Shifts
compact.keywords: Lost wage taxes; profits and new jobs
compact.zh: 税源转移：工资税减少，利润与新岗位产生税收

balanced.label: Revenue Beyond Workers’ Wages
balanced.summary: The author argues that corporate profits and robot production create other taxes, though jobs and revenues may move elsewhere.
balanced.zh: 作者认为，公司利润和机器人生产可以带来其他税收，但工作与税收可能转移到别的地区或国家。

stages.title: Earlier transport revolutions complicate the objection
stages.summary: Earlier transport changes also destroyed and created jobs; new skills mattered, and the same displaced workers did not necessarily benefit.
stages.summaryZh: 过去的交通变革也同时消灭和创造岗位；新技能很关键，而失业者本人未必能受益。

nodes.label: The historical analogy
nodes.text: Railways, cars and airlines were both job [[destroyers]] and job [[creators]].
nodes.zh: 铁路、汽车和航空既消灭旧岗位，也创造新岗位。

nodes.label: The admitted human cost
nodes.text: Those who lost work did not find the new jobs; a different set of [[skills]] filled them over time.
nodes.zh: 原先失业的人并未获得新岗位；这些岗位逐渐由具备另一套技能的人填补。

nodes.label: Why change feels more visible
nodes.text: The author argues that faster [[information]] makes today’s causes and effects more conspicuous.
nodes.zh: 作者认为，信息传播加速使今天的变化及其影响更加显眼。

compact.label: Speed in Perspective
compact.keywords: Past disruptions also demanded different skills
compact.zh: 审视速度：过去的转型同样需要不同技能

balanced.label: Earlier Transitions Also Hurt
balanced.summary: Earlier transport revolutions also displaced workers; new jobs required different skills and did not necessarily employ those who lost work.
balanced.detail: Faster information makes present changes seem more conspicuous.
balanced.zh: 早先的交通变革也使工人失业；新工作要求不同技能，未必由原先失业的人获得。作者认为，信息传播加快也使今天的变化更显眼。

stages.title: The conclusion moves from adaptation to social responsibility
stages.summary: The author concludes that automation is continuous, but restoring equilibrium is painful and calls for a humane response.
stages.summaryZh: 作者总结：自动化一直在继续，但重新达到平衡的过程很痛苦，需要以关怀回应。

nodes.label: The systemic view
nodes.text: A disrupted system takes time to reach [[equilibrium]], and the adjustment can hurt.
nodes.zh: 受到扰动的系统需要时间重新达到平衡，而调整过程会带来痛苦。

nodes.label: The ethical response
nodes.text: The current transition needs [[empathy, compassion and social responsibility]].
nodes.zh: 当前的转型需要同理心、关怀与社会责任。

compact.label: Care Through Transition
compact.keywords: Painful adjustment needs empathy and responsibility
compact.zh: 关怀转型：痛苦的调整需要同理心与责任

balanced.label: A Humane Response Matters
balanced.summary: Because transitions disrupt lives before a new equilibrium emerges, the author calls for empathy, compassion and social responsibility.
balanced.zh: 转型会在新的平衡形成前打乱人们的生活，因此作者呼吁同理心、关怀与社会责任。

compact.core: Question robot taxes; support people through change
compact.coreZh: 质疑机器人税，关怀转型中的人

balanced.route: Proposed remedy → historical and social context → tax and speed objections → humane adjustment

figure.subtitle: Debate & Mainstream Proposals → Stance · Historical & Social Perspectives → Direct Responses to the Worries → Conclusion · A Painful Transition

cards.title: Popular ideas
cards.zh: 机器人替代人的担忧，引出征税与基本收入的建议。

cards.title: Opening examples
cards.zh: 开头用盖茨的视频和欧洲议会草案，说明这些建议受到广泛关注。

cards.title: Automation as a constant
cards.zh: 作者把机器人视为工具，借纺织业说明工作形式会改变，但转型有时间差，有人会被落下。

children.text: Own pace; own tools; cottage work

cards.title: Family & demography
cards.zh: 原图的社会变化分支包括家庭、生育率和人口老龄化。文章也提出：资源限制可能促使未来一代学会节约。

cards.title: Employment · gains and limits
cards.zh: 空余人力可以投入教育、研究和医疗等领域；但作者承认收益偏向发达国家，转型也使部分人落后。

cards.title: Taxes · a changing base
cards.zh: 工资税可能减少，但作者认为公司利润会增加税收，制造机器人及投资技术也带来不同岗位；收益可能出现在其他地区。

bullets.text: Concern: unpaid robots → lower wage taxes

cards.title: Speed · historical parallels
cards.zh: 过去的交通革命既毁掉岗位又创造岗位，新岗位不一定由原失业者获得。作者认为今天的信息传播速度使变化更醒目。

cards.title: Value recap
cards.zh: 自动化贯穿历史；系统受到扰动后，需要时间重新达到平衡。

cards.title: Call to action
cards.zh: 面对当下的痛苦转型，应以同理心、同情和社会责任应对。

title: Roommates
subtitle: Remembered vitality → shared childhood and student life → a reversal of care → an inherited way of living
question: How does an apparently unchanging grandfather teach the narrator to rejoin life?
thesis: Through years of companionship and a reversal of care, the grandfather’s practical engagement with daily life becomes the narrator’s sustaining example.
thesisZh: 多年的相伴与照顾关系的反转，使祖父投入日常生活的行动，成为支撑叙述者的榜样。
conclusion: The narrator carries his grandfather’s habits into his own life, remembering an irreplaceable companion with gratitude and loss.
conclusionZh: 叙述者把祖父的生活习惯延续到自己身上，并以感激和失落追忆这位无可替代的伙伴。

design.pattern: Framed life-course with a mirrored couch: childhood → student work → adult collapse → action, returning to the opening lawn
design.rationale: 用人生阶段推进，以“本想照顾祖父却需要祖父帮助”为铰链；开头和结尾的割草、两次沙发形成回响。

stages.title: The older narrator looks back at an extraordinary roommate
stages.summary: Remembering his grandfather’s vitality, the narrator admits that he understood his own place in life only late.
stages.summaryZh: 回忆祖父旺盛的生命力时，叙述者承认自己很晚才理解在生命循环中的位置。

nodes.label: Energy taken for granted
nodes.text: His grandfather lived to [[107]] and remained capable; the narrator had always taken that energy for granted.
nodes.zh: 祖父活到107岁，始终有能力照料生活；叙述者曾把这种精力视为理所当然。

nodes.label: More than a grandparent
nodes.text: For much of his life the narrator felt like a boy beside the man who was also his [[roommate]].
nodes.zh: 在祖父面前，叙述者长久地觉得自己仍是孩子；祖父也是与他同住的室友。

compact.label: Late Understanding
compact.keywords: Grandfather's vitality once taken for granted
compact.zh: 迟来的领悟：曾把祖父的活力视为理所当然

balanced.label: A Remarkable Roommate Remembered
balanced.summary: Remembering his grandfather, who lived to 107, the narrator recognizes how slowly he understood his own place in life.
balanced.zh: 回忆活到107岁的祖父，叙述者意识到，自己很晚才理解自己在生命历程中的位置。

stages.title: Unequal attention hides a bond he later learns to hear
stages.summary: As a child he lectures an argumentative grandfather, ignores his angry dreams and only later remembers those sounds affectionately.
stages.summaryZh: 童年时，他给好争辩的祖父讲知识，排斥祖父愤怒的梦话；多年后却亲切地怀念这些声音。

nodes.label: A combative presence
nodes.text: His grandfather is no gentle old soul: he argues, shouts and remains a lover of [[strife]].
nodes.zh: 祖父并非温和的老人：他争辩、喊叫，始终热衷于冲突。

nodes.label: The boy as teacher
nodes.text: The child explains things like electricity, but his exhausted grandfather soon falls [[asleep]].
nodes.zh: 孩子向祖父解释电等知识，劳累的祖父却很快睡着。

nodes.label: A retrospective change
nodes.text: He once resisted his grandfather’s angry sleep-talk; now he remembers those outbursts as [[music]].
nodes.zh: 他曾不愿听祖父愤怒的梦话，如今却把那些喊声回忆为音乐。

compact.label: Childhood Roommates
compact.keywords: A lecturing child; an argumentative grandfather
compact.zh: 童年室友：爱讲解的孩子与好争辩的祖父

balanced.label: Childhood Lessons, Later Affection
balanced.summary: As a boy, he lectures his tired grandfather and dislikes the angry sleep-talk he later remembers affectionately.
balanced.zh: 小时候，他给疲惫的祖父讲知识，也不愿听祖父梦中的愤怒咒骂；如今却带着亲切之情回忆这些声音。

stages.title: Companionship survives a disagreement over what work means
stages.summary: Reunited during graduate school, they are congenial companions despite their different ideas about studying and working.
stages.summaryZh: 研究生时期重聚后，两人相处投契，尽管他们对学习是否算工作看法不同。

nodes.label: A companion across generations
nodes.text: After his friends have died, the grandfather joins the narrator, his most [[congenial companion]].
nodes.zh: 朋友们相继去世后，祖父搬来与最投契的伙伴——叙述者——同住。

nodes.label: Still engaged
nodes.text: He makes friends, does housework and finds plenty of political [[conflict]] to enjoy in Ann Arbor.
nodes.zh: 他结交朋友、承担家务，并在安娜堡找到许多令他兴奋的政治争论。

nodes.label: The first couch
nodes.text: Reading and underlining on the couch look like [[laziness]] to the grandfather, who mocks the narrator’s study habits.
nodes.zh: 沙发上读书和画线在祖父看来是懒惰，他因此模仿并取笑叙述者的学习方式。

compact.label: Reunited as Roommates
compact.keywords: Warm companionship; different views of work
compact.zh: 再做室友：相处融洽，对工作却看法不同

balanced.label: Companions With Different Values
balanced.summary: Reunited during graduate school, they enjoy companionship, but the grandfather mistakes reading on the couch for laziness.
balanced.zh: 研究生时期，两人再次同住，彼此投契；但祖父把他躺在沙发上读书看成懒惰。

stages.title: An established life collapses and reverses his expectations
stages.summary: He plans to support his grandfather, but his wife’s illness plunges him into depression and makes him the one needing help.
stages.summaryZh: 他原本打算照顾祖父，妻子的重病却让他陷入抑郁，成为需要帮助的人。
stages.relation: reverses the expected direction of care

nodes.label: An expected role
nodes.text: With a career and children in Texas, he intends to [[help his grandfather]] in old age.
nodes.zh: 在得克萨斯拥有事业和孩子后，他打算在祖父晚年给予照顾。

nodes.label: The reversal
nodes.text: His wife’s neurologic disease disrupts the family; anger turned inward settles into [[depression]].
nodes.zh: 妻子的神经系统疾病打乱家庭生活；他把愤怒转向自己，逐渐陷入抑郁。

nodes.label: The couch returns
nodes.text: He returns to the couch, now disconnected from work, friends and children, with nothing glorious to [[underline]].
nodes.zh: 他又躺回沙发，与工作、朋友和孩子疏远，却再也看不到值得画线赞叹的内容。

compact.label: Care Reverses
compact.keywords: Wife's illness leaves narrator needing support
compact.zh: 照顾逆转：妻子患病，叙述者反而需要支持

balanced.label: The Expected Roles Reverse
balanced.summary: After his wife becomes seriously ill, the adult who planned to support his grandfather instead withdraws into depression.
balanced.detail: The same couch now holds despair instead of study.
balanced.zh: 妻子重病后，原本打算照顾祖父的他反而陷入抑郁、与生活疏离。同一张沙发，此时承载的是绝望而非学习。

stages.title: The grandfather helps through doing rather than advice
stages.summary: His grandfather keeps caring for the household, and after about two years the narrator begins joining in daily life again.
stages.summaryZh: 祖父持续照料家庭；大约两年后，叙述者开始重新参与日常生活。
stages.relation: shows the help he actually receives

nodes.label: Work that is visible
nodes.text: At 103 and 104, the grandfather helps with the children and keeps doing the [[work of daily life]].
nodes.zh: 103岁、104岁时，祖父帮助照看孩子，继续承担眼前的日常事务。

nodes.label: An example without explanation
nodes.text: He offers neither advice nor understanding, but keeps [[doing things]] and remains engaged with life.
nodes.zh: 他没有提供劝告或理解，只是不断做事，保持对生活的投入。

nodes.label: The narrator follows
nodes.text: After about two years of melancholy, the narrator [[joins him]] and begins to see how much needs doing.
nodes.zh: 大约两年的消沉后，叙述者开始跟着祖父行动，看到生活中还有许多事情要做。

compact.label: Life Through Action
compact.keywords: Grandfather keeps helping; narrator gradually rejoins
compact.zh: 以行动生活：祖父持续付出，叙述者渐渐参与

balanced.label: Daily Work Becomes Support
balanced.summary: His grandfather cares for the children and keeps doing daily tasks; after about two years, the narrator starts joining him.
balanced.detail: He offers neither advice nor understanding, only sustained action.
balanced.zh: 祖父照顾孩子，持续做着日常事务；约两年后，叙述者开始加入。他没有提供建议或表示理解，而是始终用行动面对生活。

stages.title: The narrator’s habits preserve the lost companionship
stages.summary: He now rises early and stays busy, carrying his grandfather’s example while recognizing that such a roommate cannot be replaced.
stages.summaryZh: 如今他早起、忙碌，延续祖父的榜样，也明白这样的室友无法替代。
stages.relation: carries the example into the present

nodes.label: The inherited rhythm
nodes.text: Taking out garbage and mowing the lawn become his own way to [[stay busy]].
nodes.zh: 倒垃圾、修剪草坪，成为他自己保持忙碌的生活方式。

nodes.label: Affection and absence
nodes.text: A roommate like his grandfather comes only about once a [[century]].
nodes.zh: 祖父这样的室友，大约一个世纪才会出现一次。

compact.label: The Example Remains
compact.keywords: Early rising, daily chores, irreplaceable companionship
compact.zh: 榜样长存：早起做事，怀念无法替代的陪伴

balanced.label: An Inherited Daily Rhythm
balanced.summary: Now rising early and staying busy, the narrator carries on his grandfather’s habits while feeling the loss of his companionship.
balanced.zh: 如今，他也早起并让自己忙碌，延续祖父的生活习惯，同时感受失去这位室友后的空缺。

compact.core: Grandfather's daily example becomes a lasting inheritance
compact.coreZh: 祖父身体力行的榜样成为长久的传承

balanced.route: Present reflection → shared life → reversed dependence → practical care → inherited habits

figure.subtitle: Background of the Story → Chronological Life Story → Present Self & Final Reflection

cards.title: Present-day frame
cards.zh: 外祖父活到107岁，直到生命末期仍能割草。外孙始终觉得自己在老人面前像个孩子，“室友”关系引出回忆。

bullets.text: Narrator: still a boy beside him

cards.title: Childhood
cards.zh: 幼年阶段分为人物性格和彼此关系：老人好争辩，孩子自任老师。梦中怒骂当时令人抗拒，后来却被怀念为音乐。

cards.title: Graduate school
cards.zh: 研究生阶段，老人重新与外孙同住，交朋友、做家务。他却认为躺着读书不是工作，模仿外孙在报纸上划线。

cards.title: Established adulthood
cards.zh: 成年后的照顾关系反转：妻子患病，外孙陷入抑郁。外祖父通过照顾孩子和持续的日常行动帮助他走出低谷。

children.text: Expected helper becomes the one needing help

cards.title: Inherited living pattern
cards.zh: 外孙开始早起、保持忙碌，接过那些日常工作，继承了老人的生活方式。

bullets.text: Do the work of daily life

cards.title: Return to “roommates”
cards.zh: 结尾回扣室友意象，以感激、敬意和怀念收束；老人的生活态度延续在外孙身上。

title: Never Trust Appearances
subtitle: An ordinary train scene → a stranger’s invented biography → facts overturn the picture → stereotypes turn back on the observer
question: What happens when Matti turns a stranger’s appearance into a complete life story?
thesis: Matti’s confident portrait of a stranger collapses when facts expose the distance between observed details, national stereotypes and imaginative assumptions.
thesisZh: 事实揭示观察细节、民族刻板印象与想象推断之间的距离，马蒂自信构建的陌生人画像随之崩塌。
conclusion: The revealed identity and Geoffrey’s remarks expose Matti’s unreliable imagination and the instability of national stereotypes.
conclusionZh: 真实身份的揭晓与杰弗里的话，使马蒂不可靠的想象以及民族刻板印象的不稳固显露出来。

design.pattern: Four-act reveal with an assumption–reality mirror: ordinary scene → projected biography → contradictory facts → ironic self-recognition
design.rationale: 中部以“马蒂的猜想／揭晓的事实”成对对照，保留第8段豪车的突转；末幕以芬兰身份与花园细节反照观察者。

stages.title: A crowded setting surrounds a carefully chosen corner seat
stages.summary: Rush-hour crowds surround James Saxon, who follows a quiet routine to secure his usual corner seat.
stages.summaryZh: 晚高峰人潮包围着詹姆斯·萨克森；他按惯常安排乘车，确保坐到角落座位。

nodes.label: The public scene
nodes.text: Queues, traffic and packed trains create an atmosphere of weary [[rush-hour]] movement.
nodes.zh: 队伍、车流和拥挤的火车，构成疲惫的晚高峰场景。

nodes.label: One private routine
nodes.text: James lets the 5:14 train go and takes the 5:24 to secure his [[corner seat]].
nodes.zh: 詹姆斯放过5点14分的车，选择5点24分的车，以确保坐到角落座位。

compact.label: An Ordinary Commuter
compact.keywords: James secures his usual corner seat
compact.zh: 普通通勤者：詹姆斯坐上惯常的角落座位

balanced.label: A Quiet Commuter Observed
balanced.summary: Amid rush-hour crowds, James Saxon follows a deliberate train routine to secure a comfortable corner seat, where Matti notices him.
balanced.zh: 在下班高峰的人潮中，詹姆斯·萨克森按惯例选择车次，以占到舒适的角落座位；马蒂注意到了他。

stages.title: Observed details become national and social assumptions
stages.summary: On his first English visit, Matti treats one visible passenger as a national type and invents his occupation and family.
stages.summaryZh: 第一次到英国的马蒂，把眼前的一位乘客当作民族典型，并编出他的职业与家庭生活。

nodes.label: A national template
nodes.text: Matti measures James against a [[typical Englishman]]: umbrella, reserve and presumed cricket interest mix with mismatching features.
nodes.zh: 马蒂以“典型英国人”的模板衡量詹姆斯：雨伞、拘谨和他猜测的板球兴趣，与不符模板的外貌混杂在一起。

nodes.label: Appearance becomes status
nodes.text: Old clothes, a bulging briefcase and the initials J. S. lead him toward [[John Smith]] and an ordinary occupation.
nodes.zh: 旧衣服、鼓胀的公文包和J. S.的缩写，使他联想到“约翰·史密斯”以及普通职业。

nodes.label: Guesswork grows
nodes.text: Matti imagines a poor married man with a garden; the supposed children multiply from three to five to [[seven]].
nodes.zh: 马蒂想象对方是有花园的贫穷已婚男子；想象中的孩子从三个增加到五个，再到七个。

compact.label: Matti Imagines
compact.keywords: Poor Englishman, married, many children
compact.zh: 马蒂想象：贫穷的英国人，已婚且孩子众多

balanced.label: Observation Turns Into Invention
balanced.summary: Matti treats James as a typical Englishman, then turns old clothes and a worn briefcase into a story of poverty.
balanced.detail: His imagined family grows from three children to seven.
balanced.zh: 马蒂把詹姆斯当作典型英国人，又凭旧衣服和旧公文包想象他生活贫困；想象中的孩子从三个增加到七个。

stages.title: A chauffeur opens the door to an incompatible reality
stages.summary: A Rolls-Royce prompts Matti’s question, and Geoffrey reveals wealth, bachelorhood and Finnish origins that overturn his invented portrait.
stages.summaryZh: 劳斯莱斯引出马蒂的追问；杰弗里揭示的财富、单身身份和芬兰血统，推翻了他想象的画像。

nodes.label: The visible disruption
nodes.text: A uniformed chauffeur opens a [[Rolls-Royce]] for the man Matti thought poorly paid.
nodes.zh: 穿制服的司机为马蒂眼中收入微薄的男子打开劳斯莱斯车门。

nodes.label: Poor clerk → wealthy bachelor
nodes.text: Sir James has about [[two million pounds]], controls 42 factories and is a bachelor living in a luxury flat.
nodes.zh: 詹姆斯爵士拥有约两百万英镑，控制42家工厂，单身住在豪华公寓里。

nodes.label: English type → Finnish origins
nodes.text: His parents are [[Finnish]], his original name is Jussi Saksalainen, and he takes no interest in cricket.
nodes.zh: 他的父母都是芬兰人，原名尤西·萨克萨莱宁，而且对板球不感兴趣。

compact.label: Facts Overturn Fiction
compact.keywords: Wealthy factory owner, bachelor, Finnish origins
compact.zh: 事实推翻想象：富有的工厂老板、单身、芬兰血统

balanced.label: The Invented Portrait Collapses
balanced.summary: A chauffeur and Rolls-Royce disrupt Matti’s assumptions; Geoffrey identifies James as a wealthy bachelor whose parents are Finnish.
balanced.detail: James controls 42 factories and has no interest in cricket.
balanced.zh: 司机和劳斯莱斯打破了马蒂的判断。杰弗里说明，詹姆斯其实是父母均为芬兰人的富有单身汉，掌管42家工厂，也不喜欢板球。

stages.title: Geoffrey’s words leave Matti confronting his own imagination
stages.summary: Geoffrey mentions gardening, cricket and Finnish reserve; Matti finally remembers criticism of his overactive, unreliable imagination.
stages.summaryZh: 杰弗里提到园艺、板球和芬兰人的拘谨；马蒂终于想起老师对自己想象力过旺且不可靠的批评。

nodes.label: Familiar details return
nodes.text: Geoffrey’s gardening and shed-painting plans echo the life Matti had [[invented]] for James.
nodes.zh: 杰弗里的园艺和粉刷工具棚计划，呼应了马蒂先前为詹姆斯编造的生活。

nodes.label: A reversed national label
nodes.text: Geoffrey calls reserve [[Finnish]], unsettling the trait Matti had treated as typically English.
nodes.zh: 杰弗里把拘谨说成芬兰人的特点，动摇了马蒂先前将其视为英国人特征的判断。

nodes.label: A tentative self-correction
nodes.text: Matti concedes that his teachers may be right about his [[unreliable imagination]].
nodes.zh: 马蒂承认，老师说他的想象力不可靠，也许是对的。

compact.label: Stereotypes Unravel
compact.keywords: Finnish reserve exposes Matti's unreliable imagination
compact.zh: 刻板印象瓦解：芬兰式矜持暴露马蒂想象的不可靠

balanced.label: Matti Reconsiders His Assumptions
balanced.summary: Geoffrey calls reserve Finnish, reversing Matti’s English stereotype; Matti finally considers his teachers’ warning about his unreliable imagination.
balanced.detail: Geoffrey’s garden matches the life Matti imagined for James.
balanced.zh: 杰弗里把拘谨称为芬兰人的特征，颠倒了马蒂眼中的英国特征；他的园艺安排又呼应马蒂为詹姆斯编造的生活。马蒂终于开始认真考虑老师对自己想象力不可靠的评价。

compact.core: Facts overturn a stranger's imagined identity
compact.coreZh: 事实推翻了凭空想象的陌生人身份

balanced.route: Observed appearance → imagined identity → contradictory facts → an uneasy reconsideration of stereotypes

figure.subtitle: Setting the Scene → Matti’s Assumptions → The Truth Revealed

cards.title: Busy provincial town
cards.zh: 省城晚高峰人来人往，巴士排队、汽车拥堵、火车拥挤。

cards.title: Saxon’s quiet routine
cards.zh: 萨克森提早到站却等下一班车，只为习惯的角落座位；这种普通、安静的外表成为后面误判的起点。

cards.title: The stereotype
cards.zh: 马蒂拿心中典型英国人的模板判断眼前人：衣帽、胡须、板球、园艺、矜持等都成为依据。

bullets.text: Expected: bowler hat, fair hair, moustache

cards.title: What he actually sees
cards.zh: 他观察到的衣着与模板并不完全一致：衣服旧却整洁，头发深色，没有帽子或婚戒，公文包鼓胀。

bullets.text: Old but brushed clothes; pressed trousers

cards.title: The imagined life
cards.zh: 马蒂由衣着猜出职业、妻子和越来越多的孩子；这是想象，并非已知事实。

cards.title: New observation
cards.zh: 豪车和司机令原先的猜想站不住脚，马蒂向杰弗里追问。

cards.title: Geoffrey’s account
cards.zh: 正文说他有约200万英镑，是百万富翁而非十亿富翁；他是单身，拥有工厂、豪宅和私人飞机，父母都是芬兰人。

cards.title: Deeper understanding
cards.zh: 杰弗里的园艺、板球和“芬兰人的矜持”又把标签转向马蒂。马蒂反省想象不可靠，文章借反讽揭示外表判断的局限。

bullets.text: Labels return: gardening, cricket, Finnish reserve

title: Courage
subtitle: An unconventional arrival → a mother’s misreading → a disruptive proposal → a daughter’s resolve
question: How does a marriage proposal expose the limits of Chie’s understanding of Naomi?
thesis: Akira’s direct proposal and Naomi’s quiet resolve challenge Chie’s assumption that she can still treat the young couple as children.
thesisZh: Akira直接求婚，Naomi平静表态，挑战了Chie仍把两人视为孩子的想法。
conclusion: Naomi asserts her choice; Chie’s consent remains unresolved.
conclusionZh: Naomi明确了自己的选择；Chie是否同意，故事并未交代。

design.pattern: A four-scene narrative arc following Chie’s shifting perception, ending with Naomi’s decisive voice
design.rationale: 以Chie的视角变化串联四幕：好感、轻视、震动、误判破裂。冷雨蓝、暗玫瑰与暖纸色呼应门外与室内的张力。

stages.title: Arrival · Politeness within a breach of tradition
stages.summary: Akira bypasses convention, but his respectful manner begins to win Chie’s sympathy.
stages.summaryZh: Akira打破求婚惯例，但恭敬的举止开始赢得Chie的好感。

nodes.label: Broken convention
nodes.text: Akira comes [[directly]], rather than using a [[go-between]], on a cold, rainy winter evening.
nodes.zh: Akira在寒冷的冬日雨夜直接登门，没有通过媒人。

nodes.label: Inside the house
nodes.text: Chie is reluctant to leave the warm reading table; Naomi recognizes Akira’s name and [[urges her mother to go]].
nodes.zh: Chie不愿离开温暖的读书桌；Naomi认出Akira的名字，催母亲去见他。

nodes.label: First impression
nodes.text: The young student’s [[sincerity]] and respectful manner make Chie begin to like him and invite him inside.
nodes.zh: 年轻学生真诚而恭敬，Chie开始喜欢他，并请他进屋。

compact.label: Akira Arrives
compact.keywords: Unconventional visit, respectful manner
compact.zh: Akira登门：来访不合惯例，态度却很恭敬

balanced.label: A Respectful Rule Breaker
balanced.summary: Akira visits without a go-between; his sincere, courteous manner wins Chie’s sympathy despite the unconventional approach.
balanced.zh: 恭敬地打破惯例：Akira不经媒人直接登门，虽然不合惯例，真诚而有礼的举止仍赢得Chie的好感。

stages.title: Misreading · Chie sees children, not independent adults
stages.summary: Chie hears about America with amusement because she still views both Akira and Naomi as children.
stages.summaryZh: Chie觉得赴美的消息有些可笑，因为她仍把Akira和Naomi都当作孩子。

nodes.label: Akira’s urgency
nodes.text: Akira explains that a position serving [[Seattle’s Japanese community]] requires him to act quickly.
nodes.zh: Akira解释，给西雅图日裔社区当牙医的工作机会让他必须尽快行动。

nodes.label: Chie’s assumption
nodes.text: Chie finds his earnest speech childlike; although Naomi is eighteen, she has made [[no effort to find her a husband]].
nodes.zh: Chie觉得他认真的讲话像孩子说话；Naomi虽已十八岁，她却没有着手为女儿找丈夫。

compact.label: Chie Misjudges
compact.keywords: Still sees the couple as children
compact.zh: Chie误判：仍把这对年轻人当作孩子

balanced.label: Chie Still Sees Children
balanced.summary: Chie is amused by Akira’s earnestness because she still sees him and eighteen-year-old Naomi as children.
balanced.detail: A Seattle job offer makes his request urgent.
balanced.zh: Chie仍把两人当孩子：Akira的认真让Chie觉得好笑，因为她仍把他和十八岁的Naomi视为孩子。西雅图的工作机会使他的请求变得紧迫。

stages.title: Disruption · Two futures depend on parental consent
stages.summary: Akira reveals their understanding and offers two futures, unsettling Chie before he politely leaves.
stages.summaryZh: Akira说出两人的约定和两种未来，令Chie不安，随后礼貌告辞。
stages.relation: the real purpose overturns her view

nodes.label: A shared decision
nodes.text: Akira asks for [[Naomi’s hand]] and says they already have [[an understanding]]; Chie suddenly feels the night’s dampness.
nodes.zh: Akira请求迎娶Naomi，并说两人已有约定；Chie忽然感到夜里的湿冷。

nodes.label: Two possible homes
nodes.text: With Chie’s [[consent]], Akira will join the House of Fuji; without it, he will go to America to secure a home for his bride.
nodes.zh: 得到Chie同意，Akira便入赘Fuji家；若未获同意，他就赴美为新娘安家。

nodes.label: A courteous disruption
nodes.text: Akira apologizes and offers to return in [[two weeks]]; his departure figuratively carries away Chie’s [[ease]].
nodes.zh: Akira道歉并表示两周后可再登门；他的离去仿佛也带走了Chie的安适感。

overviewBranches.label: Parental approval
overviewBranches.caption: Stay in Japan · live in the House of Fuji

overviewBranches.label: Without approval
overviewBranches.caption: Go to America · establish a new home

compact.label: The Marriage Proposal
compact.keywords: Join Fuji; otherwise prepare their American home
compact.zh: 提出婚事：获准则加入Fuji家，否则赴美安家

balanced.label: One Proposal, Two Futures
balanced.summary: Akira proposes marriage: with Chie’s consent, he joins Naomi’s household in Japan; otherwise, he prepares their new home in America.
balanced.detail: The couple have already agreed to marry each other.
balanced.zh: 一次求婚，两种未来：Akira请求成婚；若获Chie同意，他便入赘Naomi在日本的家；否则，他将赴美为两人安家。两人早已决定结婚。

stages.title: Reversal · Expected laughter becomes a declaration
stages.summary: Chie expects Naomi to dismiss the proposal, but Naomi calmly declares her determination to marry Akira.
stages.summaryZh: Chie以为Naomi会把求婚当笑话，Naomi却平静地表明要嫁给Akira。
stages.relation: her daughter overturns the final assumption

nodes.label: What Chie expects
nodes.text: Chie calls Akira’s hopes [[preposterous]] and waits for Naomi’s [[laughter]].
nodes.zh: Chie认为Akira的愿望荒唐，并等着Naomi发笑。

nodes.label: What Naomi does
nodes.text: Naomi holds her mother’s gaze in [[silence]], then says she met Akira at her [[literary meeting]].
nodes.zh: Naomi沉默地直视母亲，然后说自己是在文学聚会上认识Akira的。

nodes.label: The final word
nodes.text: Naomi ends the exchange with [[“I mean to have him.”]] Her resolve is clear; her mother’s response is left open.
nodes.zh: Naomi以“我就是要嫁给他”结束对话。她的决心清楚明确，母亲的回应则留白。

compact.label: Naomi's Resolve
compact.keywords: Determined to marry; mother's response remains open
compact.zh: Naomi表态：决意嫁给Akira，母亲回应尚未揭晓

balanced.label: Naomi Speaks for Herself
balanced.summary: Expecting Naomi to laugh, Chie instead hears her firm intention to marry Akira; the mother’s response remains unresolved.
balanced.zh: Naomi为自己表态：Chie等着Naomi发笑，却听到女儿坚定地说要嫁给Akira；母亲会如何回应，故事留下了悬念。

compact.core: Young resolve challenges a mother's assumptions
compact.coreZh: 年轻人的决心挑战母亲的想当然

balanced.route: Unconventional arrival → maternal amusement → marriage proposal → a daughter's independent choice

cards.title: Setting & characters
cards.zh: 寒冷雨夜，Akira前来富士家。女佣开门并递上名片，原本安静的生活被打断。

cards.title: A break with convention
cards.zh: Akira直接上门，没有让母亲、父亲和媒人依传统安排；开头提出这种方式是否影响千惠接纳他的疑问。

cards.title: Before the request
cards.zh: 千惠与直美在暖炉边读书；千惠起初不愿接待，直美却催她去。Akira衣着严整、谦恭真诚，使千惠开始喜欢他。

bullets.text: Chie: cozy, reluctant → willing to receive him
Naomi: recognises his name; urges her mother

cards.title: Akira · purpose and terms
cards.zh: Akira说明西雅图的工作机会，请求娶直美并取得家长同意。同意则入赘富士家；不同意则去美国为新娘建立新家。

children.text: Become her [[yoshi]]; stay in the House of Fuji
Go to [[America]]; a new home for his [[bride]]

cards.title: Chie · emotional movement
cards.zh: 千惠从初生好感，转为把二人视作孩子的母亲式好笑；真正求婚令她感到寒意。Akira离开时带走了她的安宁，并非千惠轻松离场。

bullets.text: After his departure: her ease taken away

cards.title: Chie’s expectation
cards.zh: 千惠以为Akira的愿望荒唐，等着直美跟她一起发笑。

cards.title: Naomi’s resolve
cards.zh: 直美沉默、坚定，说明在文学聚会上认识他，并明确表示要嫁给他；母亲是否同意没有交代。

title: Reading
subtitle: Access to books → early literary ambition → accepted criticism → imitation → targeted practice
question: How does Franklin turn a love of reading into a disciplined method for learning to write?
thesis: Franklin develops as a writer by seeking books, accepting criticism, and using deliberate imitation and revision to improve expression and organization.
thesisZh: Franklin通过寻求书籍、接受批评，并有意识地模仿和修改，改善表达与篇章组织，逐渐成长为写作者。
conclusion: Repeated practice, comparison, and correction give Franklin growing confidence that he can become a competent English writer.
conclusionZh: 反复练习、比较与修改，使Franklin更有信心成为合格的英语写作者。

design.pattern: A learning pathway that expands into a workshop loop: reconstruct, compare, diagnose, practise, revise
design.rationale: 前半追踪学习资源与转折，后半放大写作训练循环；墨绿、琥珀与橄榄色区分阅读积累、诊断和练习。

stages.title: Reading · Desire meets opportunity
stages.summary: Franklin’s appetite for books shapes his apprenticeship, which brings wider access to reading.
stages.summaryZh: Franklin对书籍的热爱影响了学徒职业的选择，印刷工作又让他接触到更多书。

nodes.label: A resourceful reader
nodes.text: Franklin spends his small sums of money on books, [[sells earlier purchases]] to buy others, and reads his father’s library.
nodes.zh: Franklin把零用钱花在书上，卖掉旧书再买新书，也阅读父亲的藏书。

nodes.label: Books shape a mind
nodes.text: Plutarch’s Lives rewards his study; essays by Defoe and Mather may have influenced his [[later thinking and actions]].
nodes.zh: 阅读《名人传》使他受益；笛福和马瑟的文章可能影响了他后来的思想与行动。

nodes.label: Work opens access
nodes.text: His father chooses [[printing]] partly for his bookishness and to keep him from the sea; fellow apprentices lend him better books.
nodes.zh: 父亲因他爱书、也为阻止他出海，安排他学印刷；其他学徒借给他更好的书。

compact.label: Find Books
compact.keywords: Printing apprenticeship expands access to reading
compact.zh: 寻找书籍：印刷学徒工作拓宽阅读机会

balanced.label: Reading Creates Opportunity
balanced.summary: Franklin spends his money on books; his love of reading leads to printing, where borrowing expands his access.
balanced.zh: 阅读带来机会：Franklin把钱花在书上；爱读书使他走上印刷学徒之路，也让他能借到更多书。

stages.title: A detour · Early sales do not settle his direction
stages.summary: Borrowed books nourish literary ambition, but his father’s criticism checks Franklin’s enthusiasm for poetry.
stages.summaryZh: 借来的书滋养了文学志向，但父亲的批评抑制了Franklin写诗的热情。

nodes.label: More books, first poems
nodes.text: [[Matthew Adams]] lends Franklin books; his brother encourages occasional ballads and sends him out to sell them.
nodes.zh: Matthew Adams借书给Franklin；哥哥鼓励他写时事歌谣，并让他上街售卖。

nodes.label: Praise and discouragement
nodes.text: A recent tragedy makes his first ballad sell well, flattering his [[vanity]]; his father ridicules the poems and discourages this career.
nodes.zh: 近期发生的悲剧使第一首歌谣热卖，满足了他的虚荣心；父亲却嘲笑诗作，劝他放弃这条路。

nodes.label: A retrospective turn
nodes.text: Franklin recalls [[prose writing]] as a major means of advancement and turns to explaining how he learned it.
nodes.zh: Franklin回顾说，散文写作是自己获得发展的重要途径，接着解释他如何学习写作。

compact.label: Test Ambition
compact.keywords: Father's criticism checks enthusiasm for poetry
compact.zh: 尝试写作：父亲的批评使诗歌热情降温

balanced.label: Early Success Meets Criticism
balanced.summary: A popular ballad flatters Franklin’s vanity, but his father ridicules the poems and discourages a career in verse.
balanced.zh: 初尝成功，随后受挫：一首畅销歌谣满足了Franklin的虚荣心，但父亲嘲笑他的诗作，并劝阻他以写诗为业。

stages.title: Diagnosis · A written dispute reveals weaknesses
stages.summary: A dispute becomes a writing lesson when Franklin accepts his father’s criticism of expression, organization, and clarity.
stages.summaryZh: Franklin接受父亲对表达、组织与清晰度的批评，使一场争论变成写作课。

nodes.label: A habit with costs
nodes.text: Religious controversy encourages a [[disputatious habit]]; Franklin later recognizes its damage to conversation and friendship.
nodes.zh: 宗教论争书籍助长了爱争辩的习惯；Franklin后来认识到它会损害交谈与友谊。

nodes.label: From speech to letters
nodes.text: A debate with Collins about [[women’s education]] moves into letters after spoken argument fails to settle it.
nodes.zh: 与Collins关于女性教育的辩论未能在口头上解决，于是转为书信争论。

nodes.label: What needs improvement
nodes.text: His father praises spelling and punctuation but finds weaknesses in [[elegance, method, and perspicuity]]; Franklin accepts the diagnosis.
nodes.zh: 父亲肯定他的拼写和标点，却指出表达不够优雅、组织不够有序、意思不够清楚；Franklin接受了这些意见。

compact.label: Accept Criticism
compact.keywords: Improve expression, order, and clarity
compact.zh: 接受批评：改进表达、组织与清晰度

balanced.label: A Diagnosis He Accepts
balanced.summary: Letters debating women’s education expose weak expression, organization, and clarity; Franklin accepts his father’s criticism and resolves to improve.
balanced.zh: 接受对症的批评：关于女性教育的辩论书信暴露出表达、组织和清晰度方面的不足；Franklin接受父亲的批评，决心改进。

stages.title: A model · The Spectator becomes a practice tool
stages.summary: Franklin reconstructs admired essays from brief hints, then compares his versions with the originals and corrects faults.
stages.summaryZh: Franklin先根据简短提示重写欣赏的文章，再与原作比较并改正错误。
stages.relation: a model turns resolve into practice

nodes.label: Choose a model
nodes.text: Franklin repeatedly reads [[The Spectator]] and decides to imitate its excellent prose.
nodes.zh: Franklin反复阅读《旁观者》，决定模仿其中出色的散文。

nodes.label: Reconstruct after a delay
nodes.text: He records [[short hints]], waits several days, and rebuilds each essay without looking at the original.
nodes.zh: 他记下简短提示，隔几天后不看原文，重新写出整篇文章。

nodes.label: Diagnose through comparison
nodes.text: Comparing versions reveals faults and a shortage of [[readily usable words]], giving his next exercises a specific purpose.
nodes.zh: 比较原文与习作让他发现错误，也发现可随手调用的词汇不足，从而明确了下一步训练的目标。

compact.label: Learn by Imitation
compact.keywords: Reconstruct essays; compare and correct
compact.zh: 模仿学习：复写文章，对照原文改正

balanced.label: Reconstruct, Compare, Correct
balanced.summary: Using The Spectator as a model, he reconstructs essays from brief hints after a delay, compares versions, and corrects faults.
balanced.detail: Comparison reveals a shortage of readily available words.
balanced.zh: 重构、比较、修正：他以《旁观者》为范本，记下简短提示，隔一段时间重写文章，再与原文比较并纠错。比较让他发现自己能随时调用的词汇不足。

stages.title: A workshop · Vocabulary, order, and persistent revision
stages.summary: Targeted exercises strengthen vocabulary and organization; repeated revision and sustained effort build Franklin’s confidence.
stages.summaryZh: 针对性练习训练词汇和组织能力；反复修改与持续投入增强了Franklin的信心。

nodes.label: Vocabulary exercise
nodes.text: He turns prose tales into [[verse]], then back into prose after a delay, practising variety in word choice.
nodes.zh: 他把散文故事改写成诗，过一段时间再改回散文，以训练用词的多样性。

nodes.label: Organization exercise
nodes.text: He [[jumbles his hints]] and later restores their order before writing, learning to arrange ideas methodically.
nodes.zh: 他打乱提示，过后先重新排序再写作，以学习有条理地组织思想。

nodes.label: Revision and confidence
nodes.text: He compares and [[amends]] his work, practising around working hours and on Sundays; occasional improvements encourage his ambition.
nodes.zh: 他比较并修改习作，在工作前后和周日练习；偶尔取得的改进鼓励了他的写作志向。

compact.label: Target Weaknesses
compact.keywords: Build vocabulary, organize ideas, revise repeatedly
compact.zh: 针对弱点：积累词汇、组织思路、反复修改

balanced.label: Practice Targets Specific Weaknesses
balanced.summary: He turns prose into verse and back to expand vocabulary, then reorders shuffled hints to strengthen organization.
balanced.detail: Repeated comparison and revision build his confidence.
balanced.zh: 针对弱点反复练习：他把散文改成诗，再还原为散文，以扩充词汇；又将打乱的提示重新排序，训练篇章组织。反复比较和修改逐渐增强了他的信心。

compact.core: Better writing grows through deliberate practice
compact.coreZh: 通过有针对性的练习提升写作

balanced.route: Books awaken ambition → criticism exposes weaknesses → imitation becomes purposeful practice

figure.subtitle: Franklin as a Reader → Franklin as a Writer

cards.title: Reading lists & access
cards.zh: 富兰克林买书换书，阅读家中藏书，也向书商学徒和亚当斯借书。重要读物包括班扬、普鲁塔克、笛福和马瑟的作品。

cards.title: Influence on life
cards.zh: 阅读影响他的思维和未来经历，也让父亲为他选择印刷业；印刷工作反过来让他接触更多好书。

cards.title: Early writing & responses
cards.zh: 他写过海难和海盗题材的歌谣。公众买账，父亲却批评；他回顾散文在一生中的实用价值。

cards.title: Trigger for improvement
cards.zh: 与柯林斯辩论女性教育后通信，父亲发现他的文章拼写标点准确，但表达、条理和清晰度不足。他接受意见并努力改进。

cards.title: Main method · imitation
cards.zh: 以《旁观者》为范文：阅读、记简短提示、搁置、重写、比较、发现问题并改正。

cards.title: Additional exercises
cards.zh: 散文改成诗、再改回散文，训练词汇和提取能力；打乱提示再重排，训练思想组织，之后比较修改。

cards.title: Persistence & result
cards.zh: 他利用夜间、工作前和周日练习，逐渐学会有条理地组织思想，并相信自己能成为合格的英语作者。

bullets.text: Practice at night, before work, on Sundays

title: What We Gain or Lose in Cities
subtitle: Two urban trade-offs → contrasting civic choices → historical explanation → a reversed social comparison → an open choice
question: What benefits are worth the freedoms or social comforts that urban life may cost us?
thesis: Urban life requires compromises between personal freedom and collective interests, and between supportive social ties and liberating anonymity.
thesisZh: 城市生活需要权衡个人自由与公共利益，也需要权衡社会关系的支持和匿名生活的自由。
conclusion: No arrangement offers every benefit; the reader must weigh which compromises make urban life worth choosing.
conclusionZh: 没有一种生活安排能兼得所有好处；读者需要衡量愿意为城市生活接受哪些妥协。

design.pattern: Two comparison bands: three civic bargains, then a village–city balance that reverses its first impression
design.rationale: 第一组并排比较三地公共规则，第二组翻转乡村与城市的得失；青绿、陶土与黄铜色让收益、代价和权衡彼此可辨。

stages.title: The frame · A recent way of living with difficult choices
stages.summary: Cities are recent in human history, and their advantages come with two major kinds of compromise.
stages.summaryZh: 城市在人类历史中出现较晚，其优势伴随着两类重要的妥协。

nodes.label: Historical shift
nodes.text: Humans lived mostly in small, scattered groups; cities emerged only within the past [[6,000 years]].
nodes.zh: 人类长期主要生活在分散的小群体中；城市只在过去约六千年间出现。

nodes.label: The central claim
nodes.text: The essay examines [[individual freedom versus community interests]] and [[social ties versus anonymity]].
nodes.zh: 文章考察个人自由与公共利益，以及社会联系与匿名生活之间的权衡。

compact.label: Two Trade-offs
compact.keywords: Freedom versus community; belonging versus anonymity
compact.zh: 两组权衡：自由与集体，归属与匿名

balanced.label: Two Urban Trade-offs
balanced.summary: Urban life offers benefits at a cost: individual freedom versus community interests, and social belonging versus anonymity.
balanced.zh: 城市生活的两组权衡：城市生活的收益伴随着代价，需要权衡个人自由与公共利益，也需要权衡社会归属与匿名生活。

stages.title: Comparison one · What do rules buy a community?
stages.summary: Singapore and German cities accept restrictions for shared benefits, while Los Angeles illustrates the costs of prioritizing individual property rights.
stages.summaryZh: 新加坡和德国城市以规则换取公共利益，洛杉矶则展示了优先保护个人产权的代价。

nodes.label: Singapore · close monitoring
nodes.text: Density and vulnerability support a bargain: [[less individual freedom]] in exchange for high living standards, health, and security.
nodes.zh: 人口密集与处境脆弱促成了一种交换：以较少个人自由换取高生活水准、健康和安全。

nodes.label: Germany · shared rules
nodes.text: Rules for roofs, trees, and fishing restrict private choices while supporting [[regional character, green cities, and healthy fish populations]].
nodes.zh: 屋顶、树木和捕鱼规则限制私人选择，同时维护地方风貌、城市绿化和健康的鱼群。

nodes.label: Los Angeles · private rights
nodes.text: Sacred [[individual property rights]] coexist with lost architectural character, declining trees, environmental spillovers, and fewer fish.
nodes.zh: 被奉为神圣的个人产权，与地方建筑特色消失、树木减少、环境影响殃及邻里和鱼群减少并存。

overviewBranches.label: Singapore
overviewBranches.caption: Restrictions in return for safety and shared prosperity

overviewBranches.label: German cities
overviewBranches.caption: Limits on private choices support public benefits

overviewBranches.label: Los Angeles
overviewBranches.caption: Strong property rights, with costs for neighbours

compact.label: Freedom vs Community
compact.keywords: Singapore, Germany: rules; Los Angeles: property rights
compact.zh: 自由与集体：新加坡、德国重规则，洛杉矶重个人产权

balanced.label: What Public Rules Buy
balanced.summary: Singapore’s monitoring supports health and security; German rules protect shared surroundings, while Los Angeles’s strong property rights impose communal costs.
balanced.detail: Germany protects trees and fish; Los Angeles loses both.
balanced.zh: 公共规则换来什么：新加坡的监管维护健康与安全；德国的规则保护共同环境；洛杉矶强调个人产权，却让社会承担代价。德国保护树木和鱼群，洛杉矶的两者则在减少。

stages.title: Explanation · Cultural legacies shape present bargains
stages.summary: Different densities, urban histories, and farming traditions help explain why societies accept different balances of freedom and community.
stages.summaryZh: 人口密度、城市历史和农业传统的差异，有助于解释各社会为何接受不同的自由与公共利益平衡。

nodes.label: Density and urban history
nodes.text: The essay contrasts [[population densities]] and the differing lengths of urban history in China, Germany, and the United States.
nodes.zh: 文章比较了不同人口密度，以及中国、德国与美国城市历史的长短。

nodes.label: Inherited social arrangements
nodes.text: Communal Chinese farming, compact German farms, and scattered American frontier families leave different [[cultural legacies]].
nodes.zh: 中国的共同耕作、德国紧密相邻的农场和美国边疆分散的家庭，留下了不同的文化传统。

compact.label: Different Histories
compact.keywords: Density, farming, and settlement shape priorities
compact.zh: 历史差异：密度、农耕与定居方式影响取舍

balanced.label: Different Histories, Different Bargains
balanced.summary: Population density, urban history, and farming traditions help explain why these societies balance freedom and community differently.
balanced.zh: 历史不同，取舍不同：人口密度、城市历史和农业传统，有助于解释这些社会为何以不同方式平衡自由与公共利益。

stages.title: Comparison two · Social support versus isolation
stages.summary: New Guinea village life offers lifelong support, while moving to cities can bring isolation and weaker social ties.
stages.summaryZh: 新几内亚的乡村生活提供终身的社会支持，迁入城市却可能带来孤独和关系疏离。
stages.relation: turn to social ties and anonymity

nodes.label: Village life · support
nodes.text: Villagers are surrounded by [[lifelong friends and social support]], making traditional life seem warmly attractive.
nodes.zh: 村民身边有终身朋友和社会支持，让传统生活显得温暖而诱人。

nodes.label: City life · isolation
nodes.text: In cities, strangers and scattered friends can bring [[unhappy isolation]], diminished support, and more crime.
nodes.zh: 城市中的陌生人和分散的朋友可能意味着令人痛苦的孤独、支持减少和犯罪增多。

compact.label: Belonging
compact.keywords: Village support; city isolation
compact.zh: 归属感：乡村有支持，城市可能孤独

balanced.label: The Appeal of Belonging
balanced.summary: New Guinea villages provide lifelong friendship and support; moving to cities can leave people isolated among strangers.
balanced.zh: 归属感的吸引力：新几内亚的乡村提供终身的友谊和支持；迁入城市，却可能让人在陌生人之间感到孤立。

stages.title: Qualification · Belonging can constrain; anonymity can liberate
stages.summary: The comparison reverses when village scrutiny constrains individuals and urban anonymity offers privacy, independence, and peaceful solitude.
stages.summaryZh: 当乡村的注视限制个人，而城市匿名性带来隐私、独立与安静独处时，比较出现反转。

nodes.label: Village life · pressure
nodes.text: Constant watching and gossip can make village life [[socially suffocating]] and limit individual potential.
nodes.zh: 不断的注视和议论会让乡村生活令人窒息，限制个人潜能。

nodes.label: City life · privacy
nodes.text: A friend enjoys [[peaceful anonymity]] in a café; opaque bags and pockets let people keep small luxuries private.
nodes.zh: 一位朋友享受在咖啡馆无人打扰的匿名生活；不透明的袋子和口袋也让人能私下保有小小的享受。

compact.label: Anonymity
compact.keywords: Village scrutiny; city privacy
compact.zh: 匿名性：乡村受审视，城市提供隐私

balanced.label: The Value of Anonymity
balanced.summary: Yet village scrutiny and gossip can suffocate; urban anonymity gives people privacy and freedom from constant social demands.
balanced.detail: A friend enjoys reading undisturbed in a city café.
balanced.zh: 匿名生活的价值：然而，乡村中的监视与议论也可能令人窒息；城市的匿名性提供隐私，让人摆脱不断的人情要求。一位朋友享受在城市咖啡馆里不受打扰地读报。

stages.title: The open ending · Decide which costs are acceptable
stages.summary: The essay returns to Singapore and asks readers to weigh personal privacy against safety, health, prosperity, and pleasant surroundings.
stages.summaryZh: 文章回到新加坡的例子，请读者权衡个人隐私与安全、健康、富足及优美环境。
stages.relation: bring both trade-offs to personal judgment

nodes.label: No cost-free answer
nodes.text: Urban life comes down to [[compromises]]; the author closes with a question about the price readers would pay for shared benefits.
nodes.zh: 城市生活归根结底需要妥协；作者以问题收尾，询问读者愿为公共福祉付出什么代价。

compact.label: Your Choice
compact.keywords: Privacy or shared safety and prosperity?
compact.zh: 你的选择：隐私，还是共同的安全与繁荣？

balanced.label: Which Compromises Are Acceptable?
balanced.summary: The essay returns to Singapore, asking how much freedom readers would exchange for safety, health, prosperity, and pleasant surroundings.
balanced.zh: 哪些妥协可以接受：文章回到新加坡，询问读者愿意用多少自由，换取安全、健康、富足与优美环境。

compact.core: Urban gains come with personal compromises
compact.coreZh: 城市生活的收益伴随着个人的取舍

balanced.route: Two trade-offs → contrasting civic choices → village–city reversal → personal judgment

figure.subtitle: Introduction → Trade-off One · Freedom & Community → Trade-off Two · Social Ties & Anonymity → Conclusion · What Would You Choose?

cards.title: Three time periods
cards.zh: 从人类长期低密度生活，到六千年前出现城市，再到如今多数人住在城市，时间推进为得失问题铺垫。

bullets.text: Most human history: scattered families / bands
Today: more than half live in cities

cards.title: Thesis · two trade-offs
cards.zh: 文章提出两条独立主线：个人自由与公共利益，社会联系与匿名生活。

cards.title: Singapore
cards.zh: 依照原图“为什么—怎么做—结果”的分支：新加坡地域小、人口密集且依赖邻国，因此密切监控居民，以较少自由换取健康、安全和生活水平。

children.text: Dense population; tiny territory; dependence on neighbours
Inspectors check water; sensors monitor daily life

cards.title: Germany
cards.zh: 德国城市也人口密集，规则保护公共环境。屋顶、树木和捕鱼都有约束，换来美好建筑、绿城、艺术支持和健康鱼群。

children.text: Roof rules; tree protection; strict [[fishing]] licences
Architecture; green cities; arts; healthy fish

cards.title: Los Angeles
cards.zh: 洛杉矶以个人产权为重，共同限制较少，却导致建筑风格杂乱、树木减少、升温、污染殃及邻居、鱼群衰退。

children.text: Few shared restrictions; easy fishing permits
Tree loss; heat; pollution spillover; fewer fish

cards.title: Why societies choose differently
cards.zh: 原图把这一段作为解释层：地理、人口密度、城市历史和农业模式造成不同文化遗产，说明各地取舍为何不同。

cards.title: First view · ties as support
cards.zh: 起初，村落里的终身朋友和社会支持显得温暖，城市生活却可能让迁居者孤独、朋友分散并失去支持。

bullets.text: Initial attraction: the warmth of village life

cards.title: Reconsideration · anonymity as freedom
cards.zh: 随后翻转视角：村落里的监视、议论和族人索求会压抑个体，城市匿名性则提供独处、隐私与自主。

bullets.text: Qualification: both places have gains and costs

cards.title: Return to Singapore
cards.zh: 文章回到新加坡：为了安全、健康、富裕和美好环境，我们愿意接受何种监控？结尾要求权衡，并没有指定统一答案。

bullets.text: An open choice, not one universal answer

title: The Guide to Being a Foodie Without Being Culturally Appropriative
subtitle: A personal contradiction leads to a power-based definition, three areas of scrutiny, and a call to connect food with people.
question: When does enjoying another culture’s food become an unequal exercise of power?
thesis: Food appropriation involves unequal power: cultures become spectacles or products while their histories, communities, and access to food are disregarded.
thesisZh: 食物挪用涉及不平等的权力：文化被变成奇观或商品，而其历史、社群及获取食物的机会遭到忽视。
conclusion: Enjoy food across cultures while examining who benefits, respecting its communities, and learning about the conditions that shape their lives.
conclusionZh: 可以享受跨文化饮食，同时追问谁获利、尊重来源社群，并了解塑造其生活处境的因素。

design.pattern: Definition trunk → three parallel scrutiny branches → ethical response
design.rationale: 以定义为主干，把文化表述、历史社群、资源利益分为并行审视分支，再汇入行动；陶土、橄榄、谷物金呼应食物与土地。

stages.title: Childhood food becomes an exotic restaurant trend
stages.summary: The author contrasts ridicule of her childhood food with its fashionable, expensive reinvention by others.
stages.summaryZh: 作者把童年食物遭到嘲笑的经历，与他人将其重新包装成昂贵潮流的现象并置。

nodes.label: Media spectacle
nodes.text: Cooking shows frame familiar foods such as century eggs and stinky tofu as [[exotic]] or bizarre.
nodes.zh: 烹饪节目把皮蛋、臭豆腐等熟悉的食物呈现为异国奇物或怪异食材。

nodes.label: A continent on a menu
nodes.text: “Asian-inspired” and “Asian-fusion” labels combine a vast, diverse continent into a broad restaurant [[category]].
nodes.zh: “亚洲风味”和“亚洲融合”的标签把广阔、多样的亚洲归入宽泛的餐饮类别。

nodes.label: From ridicule to trend
nodes.text: Food once mocked now appears as $16 Spam fried rice: the change raises questions about [[appropriation]].
nodes.zh: 曾受嘲笑的食物如今成为售价16美元的午餐肉炒饭；这种变化引出文化挪用的问题。

compact.label: Double Standards
compact.keywords: Mocked childhood food becomes expensive fashion
compact.zh: 双重标准：童年被嘲笑的食物变成昂贵潮流

balanced.label: Mocked Food Becomes Fashion
balanced.summary: The author's childhood foods, once ridiculed, reappear as exotic television ingredients and expensive dishes marketed by others.
balanced.detail: Spam fried rice now sells for $16.
balanced.zh: 被嘲笑的食物成为潮流：作者童年吃的食物曾受嘲笑，如今却被他人包装成电视里的异国食材和昂贵菜肴。午餐肉炒饭如今卖到16美元。

stages.title: Enjoyment becomes problematic through unequal power
stages.summary: The author distinguishes cultural enjoyment from dominant groups’ fetishization, commercialization, and control of another community’s food.
stages.summaryZh: 作者区分了文化欣赏与支配群体对其他社群食物的猎奇化、商业化及控制。

nodes.label: Enjoyment is allowed
nodes.text: Eating dumplings or noodles from another culture does not automatically amount to [[appropriation]].
nodes.zh: 吃另一种文化的饺子或面条，并不自动构成文化挪用。

nodes.label: The author’s definition
nodes.text: A [[dominant culture]] adopts parts of a culture whose people it has oppressed, enjoying them without sharing that oppression.
nodes.zh: 支配文化采用其所压迫群体的文化元素，享受它们，却无需承受相同的压迫。

nodes.label: Three warning signs
nodes.text: [[Fetishization]], commercialization, and hoarding access can reduce communities to cuisine and place resources under outsiders’ control.
nodes.zh: 猎奇化、商业化和垄断获取机会，可能把社群简化为菜肴，并让外来者掌控相关资源。

compact.label: Where Appropriation Begins
compact.keywords: Unequal power, commercialization, control
compact.zh: 挪用的边界：权力不平等、商业化与控制

balanced.label: Enjoyment Versus Unequal Power
balanced.summary: Appreciation becomes appropriation when a dominant culture fetishizes, commercializes, or controls the food of communities it has oppressed.
balanced.zh: 欣赏与不平等权力的边界：当支配文化把曾受其压迫的社群食物猎奇化、商业化或加以控制时，欣赏便成为挪用。

stages.title: Labels and authenticity can flatten living cultures
stages.summary: Selective ethnic labels and fixed ideas of authenticity erase cultural diversity and the complicated histories of food.
stages.summaryZh: 选择性使用的族裔标签和固定的正宗观念，抹去了文化多样性与食物的复杂历史。

nodes.label: Who counts as “ethnic”?
nodes.text: The author finds “ethnic” reserved for cuisines perceived as [[foreign]] to White diners, although Western European cuisines also have ethnic roots.
nodes.zh: 作者发现，“族裔食物”通常专指白人食客眼中的异域菜肴，尽管西欧菜肴也有族裔根源。

nodes.label: A region reduced to dishes
nodes.text: Reducing Japan to sushi or India to curry produces [[homogenization]], concealing the diversity of their communities.
nodes.zh: 把日本简化为寿司、把印度简化为咖喱，会造成同质化，遮蔽当地社群的多样性。

nodes.label: Authenticity freezes a moving history
nodes.text: The author links Spam dishes to colonial history; seeking a timeless [[authenticity]] overlooks how food cultures travel and change.
nodes.zh: 作者把午餐肉菜肴与殖民历史联系起来；追寻恒久不变的“正宗”，会忽视饮食文化的流动与变化。

compact.label: Culture Reduced
compact.keywords: Labels erase diversity and changing histories
compact.zh: 文化被简化：标签抹去多样性与变化的历史

balanced.label: Culture Reduced to Menus
balanced.summary: Ethnic labels flatten diverse communities; fixed ideas of authenticity overlook how food traditions travel and change.
balanced.detail: Japan becomes sushi; Spam carries colonial history.
balanced.zh: 文化被简化为菜单：族裔标签抹平社群的多样性，固定的正宗观念忽略饮食传统的流动与变化。日本被简化为寿司；午餐肉则承载殖民历史。

stages.title: Enjoyable dishes can be detached from community realities
stages.summary: Enjoying food while ignoring its communities separates pleasure from histories of migration, colonization, and present oppression.
stages.summaryZh: 享受食物却忽视其社群，会把饮食乐趣与移民史、殖民史及当下的压迫割裂。

nodes.label: Present concerns disappear
nodes.text: Loving Mexican food can coexist with indifference to [[labor rights]] and immigration policies affecting Mexican communities.
nodes.zh: 喜爱墨西哥食物，仍可能与漠视影响墨西哥社群的劳工权利和移民政策并存。

nodes.label: Historical connections disappear
nodes.text: Kung Pao chicken and curry carry stories of [[immigration]] and colonialism; consuming only their pleasurable parts leaves those stories out.
nodes.zh: 宫保鸡丁和咖喱承载着移民与殖民历史；只消费令人愉快的部分，会遗漏这些故事。

compact.label: People Forgotten
compact.keywords: Enjoying cuisine while ignoring its communities
compact.zh: 群体被遗忘：享用美食，却忽略其背后的人

balanced.label: Food Without Its People
balanced.summary: Loving Mexican food while ignoring immigration and labor issues shows how cuisine becomes detached from its communities.
balanced.zh: 食物与其社群脱节：喜爱墨西哥食物却忽视移民和劳工问题，说明饮食如何与其来源社群割裂。

stages.title: Commercial reinvention can exclude the source community
stages.summary: Upscale restaurants and repackaged ingredients can profit from community foods while making those foods less accessible to their original communities.
stages.summaryZh: 高档餐厅和重新包装的食材可能从社群食物中获利，同时让来源社群更难获得自己的食物。

nodes.label: Affordable food becomes luxury
nodes.text: Chefs elevate inexpensive community dishes into restaurants their source communities may find [[inaccessible]]; the author distinguishes this from communities reworking their own traditions.
nodes.zh: 厨师把社群的廉价菜肴升级为来源社群可能无法进入的高档餐饮；作者将此与社群改造自身传统加以区分。

nodes.label: Questions for chefs and diners
nodes.text: Ask who is [[laboring and profiting]], where recipes originate, and whether historically oppressed groups supply the cuisine.
nodes.zh: 追问谁在劳动、谁在获利，食谱来自哪里，以及这些菜肴是否出自历史上受压迫的群体。

nodes.label: Traditional food becomes unaffordable
nodes.text: The author calls exclusion through rising prices [[food gentrification]], using repackaged ingredients, including quinoa, to illustrate the concern.
nodes.zh: 作者把价格上涨造成的排斥称为食物绅士化，并以藜麦等重新包装的食材说明这一忧虑。

compact.label: Who Benefits?
compact.keywords: Outsiders profit; rising prices exclude communities
compact.zh: 谁获益：外人获利，涨价使原有群体难以享用

balanced.label: Who Profits, Who Loses?
balanced.summary: Upscale restaurants and repackaged ingredients enrich outsiders while rising prices can exclude the communities whose foods they sell.
balanced.zh: 谁获利，谁受损：高档餐厅和重新包装的食材使外来者获利，涨价却可能让来源社群无法再享用自己的食物。

stages.title: Keep enjoying food while examining power
stages.summary: The conclusion permits cross-cultural enjoyment while urging reflection on power and education about the communities behind each meal.
stages.summaryZh: 结尾认可跨文化饮食的乐趣，同时要求反思权力，并了解每顿饭背后的社群。

nodes.label: Retain cross-cultural enjoyment
nodes.text: The author enjoys food beyond her own culture; the problem is food’s potential use as a tool of [[oppression]].
nodes.zh: 作者也喜欢其他文化的食物；问题在于食物可能被用作压迫的工具。

nodes.label: Examine the relationship
nodes.text: Reflect on how cultures are perceived and on the relationship between [[food, people, and power]].
nodes.zh: 反思人们如何看待所消费的文化，以及食物、人与权力之间的关系。

nodes.label: Learn beyond the meal
nodes.text: Learn about [[colonization]], gentrification, and current issues affecting the communities from which meals come.
nodes.zh: 了解殖民化、绅士化，以及影响食物来源社群的当下问题。

compact.label: Enjoy With Awareness
compact.keywords: Learn histories; question power; respect communities
compact.zh: 有意识地享用：了解历史、审视权力、尊重群体

balanced.label: Reconnect Food and People
balanced.summary: Keep enjoying cross-cultural food, but ask who benefits and learn about the communities, histories, and power relations behind meals.
balanced.zh: 重新连接食物与人：继续享受跨文化饮食，同时追问谁获益，了解餐食背后的社群、历史与权力关系。

compact.core: Food appreciation must consider people and power
compact.coreZh: 欣赏美食也要关注其背后的群体与权力

balanced.route: Personal contradiction → unequal power → representation, community, and access → responsible enjoyment

figure.subtitle: Observation → Question → Thesis → Mechanisms → Consequences → Solutions · Attitude & Action

cards.title: Personal observation
cards.zh: 从童年食物被嘲笑，到成为昂贵的时尚餐饮，作者以亲历反差开启讨论。

cards.title: The question
cards.zh: 什么是饮食中的文化挪用？作者首先区分跨文化欣赏和挪用，单纯享受别人的食物并不等于挪用。

bullets.text: Eating another culture’s food ≠ automatically harmful

cards.title: Thesis · people with power
cards.zh: 挪用发生在主导文化利用受压迫群体的食物，将其迷恋化、商业化，或控制获取渠道时；关键是权力关系。

cards.title: Fetishization
cards.zh: “异国”“民族风味”和固定的“正宗”想象，把文化化作可消费的奇观，遮蔽变化、殖民历史和内部差异。

bullets.text: Culture treated as a consumable spectacle

cards.title: Commercialization
cards.zh: 高档厨师重新包装原本便宜的社区食物，原社区却未必能进入或从中获益。作者要求追问谁付出劳动、谁获利。

bullets.text: Different from communities adapting their own food

cards.title: Access hoarding
cards.zh: 企业重新包装原料，将藜麦、椰子等变成时尚商品；原社区可能失去可负担的食物获取渠道。

bullets.text: Examples: quinoa; coconut water; collard greens

cards.title: Cultural flattening
cards.zh: 整个地区被简化成菜单标签，内部社区、历史与差异被抹平。

bullets.text: Whole regions reduced to menu items

cards.title: Disconnection
cards.zh: 人们只取用美味的部分，却忽略食物背后的劳动、移民历史及相关群体承受的压迫。

bullets.text: Food detached from people and history

cards.title: Gentrification
cards.zh: 当原社区负担不起自己的饮食、无法维持传统时，文章称之为食物中产阶级化。食物也可能成为压迫工具。

bullets.text: Communities priced out of their own cuisines

cards.title: Attitude
cards.zh: 作者并不反对跨文化饮食，而是要求有意识地欣赏，反思自己如何看待他人文化。

bullets.text: Reflect on how cultures are perceived

cards.title: Action
cards.zh: 行动在于了解食物、人和权力的关系，学习食物来源社区面临的现实问题，以及殖民和中产阶级化的影响。

title: Stop Telling Me to Travel like a Local, Okay?
subtitle: The local myth is challenged, the tourist’s advantages are recovered, and the same curious outlook returns home.
question: What do we gain by openly being tourists, abroad and at home?
thesis: The ideal of traveling like a local misunderstands ordinary local life and undervalues the curiosity, learning, hospitality, and freedom available to tourists.
thesisZh: “像当地人旅行”的理想误解了当地人的日常生活，也低估了游客所拥有的好奇、学习机会、款待与自由。
conclusion: Embrace being a tourist with humility and respect, then bring the same curiosity and urgency to everyday life at home.
conclusionZh: 以谦逊和尊重接受游客身份，再把同样的好奇与行动热情带回家乡的日常生活。

design.pattern: Myth → rebuttal → three tourist advantages → a return-home turn
design.rationale: 先设置反常识论点，再让学习、款待、自由作为游客身份的并列价值，末端回转到家乡；蓝、橙、青绿体现旅行的开阔与活力。

stages.title: A self-aware tourist rejects a fashionable instruction
stages.summary: The author embraces her tourist identity and challenges the apparently attractive promise of traveling like a local.
stages.summaryZh: 作者坦然接受游客身份，并质疑“像当地人旅行”这一看似诱人的承诺。

nodes.label: The author’s own practice
nodes.text: She uses the knowledge of people who know a place well and deliberately visits its [[only-here]] highlights.
nodes.zh: 她借助熟悉当地者的知识，并有意识地游览当地独有的精华景点。

nodes.label: The fashionable promise
nodes.text: “Travel like a local” offers the [[inside scoop]] while advice about hiding tourist identity makes unfamiliarity seem shameful.
nodes.zh: “像当地人旅行”承诺提供内行资讯，而掩饰游客身份的建议让人生地不熟显得可耻。

nodes.label: The counterclaim
nodes.text: The promise sounds attractive, but the author calls it a [[paradoxical myth]] and potentially terrible vacation advice.
nodes.zh: 这个承诺听起来诱人，作者却称其为自相矛盾的迷思，甚至可能是糟糕的度假建议。

compact.label: Question the Slogan
compact.keywords: Traveling like a local is overrated
compact.zh: 质疑口号：“像当地人旅行”被过度推崇

balanced.label: Reject the Local Performance
balanced.summary: The author embraces being a tourist and challenges advice that makes visitors ashamed of their unfamiliarity with a place.
balanced.zh: 拒绝扮演当地人：作者坦然接受游客身份，反对让访客因不熟悉一个地方而感到羞耻的旅行建议。

stages.title: Daily routines expose the contradiction
stages.summary: Locals’ work and chores differ from the sightseeing, special meals, and fresh attention that make a holiday valuable.
stages.summaryZh: 当地人的工作和家务，与让假期富有价值的观光、特色餐饮和新鲜目光并不相同。
stages.relation: test the claim against everyday life

nodes.label: Ordinary local life
nodes.text: Locals work, commute, run errands, and watch television; travel offers escape from this [[everyday routine]].
nodes.zh: 当地人工作、通勤、办杂事、看电视；旅行则让人暂时离开这种日常惯例。

nodes.label: A stay does not make identity
nodes.text: A neighborhood Airbnb does not make someone a local, and constant elaborate meals are no model of ordinary [[local life]].
nodes.zh: 住进社区里的民宿并不会让人成为当地人，连续享用精致大餐也不是普通当地生活的样板。

nodes.label: The visitor’s distinctive pleasures
nodes.text: Museums, boat tours, regional textiles, and wandering with [[fresh eyes]] are pleasures the author urges tourists to enjoy.
nodes.zh: 博物馆、游船、地方纺织品，以及带着新鲜目光漫步，都是作者鼓励游客享受的乐趣。

compact.label: Ordinary Local Life
compact.keywords: Work and chores differ from holiday pleasures
compact.zh: 当地人的日常：工作家务不同于度假的乐趣

balanced.label: Locals Have Everyday Lives
balanced.summary: Locals work, commute, and do chores; tourists escape those routines to explore museums, landmarks, and unfamiliar streets.
balanced.detail: A neighborhood Airbnb does not make someone a local.
balanced.zh: 当地人也有日常生活：当地人工作、通勤、做家务；游客则离开这些常规，探索博物馆、地标和陌生街道。住进社区里的民宿，并不会使人成为当地人。

stages.title: Acknowledging unfamiliarity makes room for expertise
stages.summary: Admitting limited knowledge allows visitors to learn more through guides, cooking classes, and explanations of unfamiliar practices.
stages.summaryZh: 承认知识有限，使游客能从导览、烹饪课以及对陌生习俗的讲解中学到更多。

nodes.label: Admit the starting point
nodes.text: Getting more from a visit requires acknowledging [[ignorance and vulnerability]] and accepting that help may be needed.
nodes.zh: 要从旅行中获得更多，就需要承认自己的无知和脆弱，并接受自己可能需要帮助。

nodes.label: Let local knowledge deepen experience
nodes.text: Guided markets and cooking classes offer [[expertise]] that explains ingredients and practices a visitor cannot simply intuit.
nodes.zh: 市场导览和烹饪课程提供专业知识，解释游客无法单靠直觉理解的食材与做法。

compact.label: Learn as Beginners
compact.keywords: Admit unfamiliarity; welcome guides and classes
compact.zh: 以初学者学习：承认陌生，接受导览与课程

balanced.label: Let Local Knowledge Help
balanced.summary: Admitting ignorance enriches the visit: expert guides explain ingredients and practices that tourists cannot simply understand on their own.
balanced.zh: 借助当地知识：承认自己的无知会丰富旅程；专业导游能解释游客无法独自领会的食材与当地做法。

stages.title: Being a visitor can invite unexpected generosity
stages.summary: Personal encounters in Thailand, Kyoto, and Paris illustrate the hospitality visitors can receive when they seek help.
stages.summaryZh: 泰国、京都和巴黎的亲身经历，展示了游客求助时可能获得的款待。

nodes.label: Thailand · directions become a ride
nodes.text: After a request for directions, a café owner closes her shop and offers a motorbike ride to a rice noodle factory: unexpected [[kindness]].
nodes.zh: 作者只是问路，咖啡店主却关店骑摩托车送她去米粉厂，展现出意外的善意。

nodes.label: Kyoto · a question opens a home
nodes.text: Asking about ceramics leads to an invitation to learn [[kintsugi]] in a couple’s home.
nodes.zh: 询问陶瓷店的位置，换来了到一对夫妇家中学习金缮的邀请。

nodes.label: Paris · welcome deserves gratitude
nodes.text: Friends enthusiastically lead her between food shops in Paris; she urges visitors to accept [[hospitality]] with gratitude rather than shame.
nodes.zh: 朋友们热情地带她逛巴黎的食品店；她主张游客以感激而非羞耻接受款待。

compact.label: Accept Hospitality
compact.keywords: Seeking help can invite unexpected kindness
compact.zh: 接受款待：开口求助，可能收获意外善意

balanced.label: Vulnerability Can Invite Hospitality
balanced.summary: Asking for help can bring unexpected welcome: a Kyoto ceramics inquiry becomes an invitation to learn kintsugi at a couple's home.
balanced.zh: 示弱可能带来款待：求助可能换来意外的欢迎；在京都询问陶瓷店，竟让作者受邀到一对夫妇家里学习金缮。

stages.title: Drop the performance of fitting in
stages.summary: Travel frees visitors from anxiety about appearances, while respect for local religious and cultural customs remains necessary.
stages.summaryZh: 旅行让游客不必为外表和融入而焦虑，但仍须尊重当地的宗教和文化习俗。

nodes.label: Release the pressure to fit in
nodes.text: Because strangers do not know you, travel’s [[anonymity]] makes it easier to dress practically and ask for directions.
nodes.zh: 由于陌生人不认识你，旅行的匿名性让人更自在地穿着实用衣物、开口问路。

nodes.label: Keep the cultural boundary
nodes.text: Not worrying about looking foreign still requires respecting local [[customs]], including religious and cultural dress expectations.
nodes.zh: 不再担心看起来像外国人，仍需要尊重当地习俗，包括宗教和文化对着装的要求。

compact.label: Relax With Respect
compact.keywords: Drop appearance anxiety; honor local customs
compact.zh: 自在而尊重：放下外表焦虑，尊重当地习俗

balanced.label: Release the Need to Fit
balanced.summary: Anonymity lets tourists dress practically and ask directions freely, while respect for local religious and cultural customs remains essential.
balanced.zh: 放下融入的压力：身处无人认识自己的地方，游客可以穿得实用、自在问路，同时仍须尊重当地的宗教与文化习俗。

stages.title: The argument turns from travel to everyday life
stages.summary: The author reverses the slogan: a tourist’s curiosity and urgency can counter the complacency of living near familiar places.
stages.summaryZh: 作者反转了口号：游客的好奇与行动热情，可以对抗人们对身边熟悉地方的漫不经心。
stages.relation: extend the argument into daily life

nodes.label: Familiarity encourages postponement
nodes.text: The author admits neglecting nearby landmarks and walks; believing places will always be there can breed [[apathy]].
nodes.zh: 作者承认自己忽略了附近的地标和步道；以为它们永远在那里，会滋生冷漠。

nodes.label: Make the visit happen
nodes.text: Take a local tour, enter a museum, or explore a nearby trail: [[tourist energy]] brings curiosity and action into ordinary life.
nodes.zh: 参加本地游览、走进博物馆或探索附近步道：游客的热情把好奇和行动带入普通生活。

compact.label: Bring Curiosity Home
compact.keywords: Explore familiar places with tourist energy
compact.zh: 把好奇带回家：用游客的热情探索熟悉之地

balanced.label: Bring Tourist Curiosity Home
balanced.summary: The argument turns homeward: use a tourist's curiosity and urgency to visit nearby places instead of postponing them indefinitely.
balanced.zh: 把游客的好奇带回家：论述转向家乡；用游客的好奇与行动热情探索身边的地方，而不是无限推迟。

compact.core: Embrace being a tourist; keep the curiosity
compact.coreZh: 坦然做游客，并把好奇心带回生活

balanced.route: Challenge the local ideal → recover tourist advantages → bring curiosity home

cards.zh: 维也纳和柬埔寨的旅行回忆引出作者坦然承认的游客身份。

cards.title: Her tourist wisdom
cards.zh: 短暂旅行依赖熟悉当地者的经验，选择只能在此地体验的经典景点，不必伪装本地人。

cards.title: Phenomenon & promise
cards.zh: “像当地人一样旅行”的口号许诺内部消息和避开旅游陷阱，却常带有羞辱游客身份的意味。

bullets.text: Promise: insider tips; no tourist traps
Pressure: do not look or act like a visitor

cards.title: Why it is a farce
cards.zh: 作者指出当地人并不在旅行，而是在工作和处理家务，因此口号本身自相矛盾。

bullets.text: An Airbnb does not create a local identity

cards.title: The pleasures of tourism
cards.zh: 游客可以逛博物馆、游船、买手工艺品，用新鲜眼光探索地方；旅行本来就是离开日常琐碎。

cards.title: Humility → learning
cards.zh: 承认无知和脆弱，再通过烹饪课、市场导览和专家解释去学习；态度自然转为行动。

cards.title: Vulnerability → connection
cards.zh: 求助带来好客与人际联系：泰国人骑车带路、京都邀请学金缮、巴黎朋友热情引领；应怀着感激接受。

bullets.text: Thailand: ride; Kyoto: kintsugi; Paris: food shops

cards.title: Anonymity → freedom
cards.zh: 旅行让人暂时摆脱日常社交目光，不必执着融入；穿舒适衣服、问路即可，但仍须尊重当地文化习俗。

cards.title: Practice · do, do not defer
cards.zh: 把游客式行动带回家乡：乘巴士游览、真正去博物馆、访问附近地标，而不是一直推迟。

bullets.text: Take a bus tour; visit museums and landmarks

cards.title: Reason · renewed attention
cards.zh: 熟悉容易导致漠然和拖延；游客的紧迫感则唤回好奇和新鲜眼光。
